item.title: Fritz Neumann Exhibition 1978/1979
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
It was more of a chance discovery: While conducting a routine search for previously unrecorded works by Ric or Fritz Neumann, I came across this exhibition catalog by Fritz Neumann. The images from the last post included some information about the painting’s provenance.

Apparently, a sales exhibition of watercolors by Fritz Neumann took place from November 9, 1978, to January 2, 1979. The venue listed is the Siemenshaus at Salzufer 6–8 in Berlin. This is a former telephone factory (German).

item.title: Hedwig Klinge in the Fine Art Collection Schmelzle
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Since the identity of Fritz Neumann has been clarified and the extracts from the civil registers are known, we know about his wife Hedwig Klinge. Since the beginning of the year, some examples of her work can be found in this blog.

Now Peter Schmelzle has come forward. Since 2018, he has been searching for the person behind the signature ‘Klinge’. He also asked his readers to send in examples of corresponding graphics and thus created a small collection of examples of graphics by Hedwig Klinge. He recently became aware of the contribution with the etching of a magnolia and was thus able to clarify the identity.

item.title: Article on Fritz Neumann in Spandauer Volksblatt 19.2.1972 - Text
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
The article “Segelboote für Millionäre und Vögel für sich selbst” (Sailboats for millionaires and birds for themselves) by Uwe-Michael Troppenz from the previous post , published in the Spandauer Volksblatt on 19 February 1972, archive shelfmark IV C Z ZA PA 1038 (Archive of the Spandau City History Museum).

Transcription

Fritz Neumann: “My favourite thing to paint is what I see …

Sailboats for millionaires and birds for himself

Fritz Neumann is the opposite of Erich Wladimir Weger. But when Weger calls for a political painter, Neumann shakes his head: “A painter doesn’t have to be political at all.” And where Weger tries to provoke the viewer with the red colour, Neumann paints purple because purple is modern, it sells better - “in the past I would probably have used green-blue.” While Weger dreams of realising his ideas, Neumann strives to make the sailing boats of millionaires as lifelike as possible.

Admittedly, it would be unfair to accuse Fritz Neumann of disdainful materialism. Because he likes to paint what he has to paint. The secret of freedom. His watercolours and etchings range stylistically from naturalism to cubism and abstract motifs. Although the cubist paintings, reminiscent of Feininger the sailor, are of artistic merit and hint at inspirations that point beyond the façade of the recognisable, Neumann explains: “I prefer to paint what I see.” What he sees are sailing boats.

And so different styles coexist on an equal footing in his paintings. As a sail painter, Neumann - as he says himself - has little competition to fear. For this reason, and because of his own enthusiasm for water sports, the boats on the Havel are his professional motif. But he also has a private motif: birds, ripe for scientific illustrations. That’s probably what those responsible at the “Deutsche Allgemeine Zeitung” thought at the time when they recruited Fritz Neumann as an employee.

Fritz was born into the imperial world in December 1897 and had the misfortune of having a father who did not give him an artist’s name. Neumann. But talent is ultimately the deciding factor, and so the gifted teenager enjoyed an art school education from 1912 to 1916, the tween was in the trenches of Verdun during the First World War, ran an advertising studio after his return home and then decided to become a freelance painter and etcher in 1930. Neumann was involved in the Second World War right from the start, but it wasn’t so bad for him: “I painted more during the war than I fought. My company commander was a professor, and he was very understanding.”

After the Second World War, he switched from the drypoint technique to the etching technique for his etchings. The Spandau Art Office wrote last summer that Neumann had “a strictly composed cathedral style. The influence of earlier years is unmistakable in his use of glass mosaic”. The artist commented that the copper etching itself to a certain extent prescribes a strict style, stylising the motif.

Strict or not strict Artist Neumann can make a good living from his paintings, which are sold by the art collections Amsler & Ruthardt and Vagart & Co. Sailing boats for the millionaires, Spandau motifs “for the people” and birds for himself.

However, Mrs Hedwig Neumann, who met her husband at art school, was taken with flora. She painted radiant sunflowers under her maiden name Hede Klinge. She also works for a publisher, but does not compete with her husband. Hede Klinge does not paint sailboats.

• When Fritz Neumann sits in Bocksfelde and observes the Havel, swiftly running his brush over the canvas on his easel, he likes it when curious travellers debate the problems of art with the master - problems that Fritz Neumann does not have. He brought back impressions and sketches from his long journeys, which he repeatedly returned to in charcoal and pastel: Sturdy fishing boats in Greece, ships on the canals in Venice, at the pier in Cuxhaven or Amsterdam, on the rivers of Paris.

He can’t let it go, it has taken hold of him, once and for all, definitively, irrevocably. And the buyers appreciate the fact that Fritz Neumann is a professional and knows exactly what the rigging should look like. That is very useful.

UWE-MICHAEL TROPPENZ

Fritz Neumann and his sailing boats: “I like to paint what I have to paint”, he says. (Pictures: Franke)

item.title: Civil register entries for Fritz Neumann
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Thanks to Torsten Steinberg, we now have two civil register entries for Fritz Neumann. These are partly the source for the dates in the main entry .

Marriage certificate

This is the marriage certificate of Franz Robert Fritz Neumann and Anna Hedwig Klinge, married on 2 May 1925. The occupation of both is given as “draughtsman” and “draughtswoman”.

Fritz Neumann’s birthday is given as 6 December 1897 and his address as Lettestraße 1.

item.title: Fritz Neumann in the "Catalog of Copyright Entries"
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description: The United States Copyright Office (USCO) is a keeper of differend kind of copyright entries. It used to issue a printed catalogue of those registered copyright claims. Since the USA has been a global market already before world war two, there were copyright registrations by J.C. Blumenberg in the thirties. Some of those, especially in Part 4: Works of Art, these also cover works by our Fritz Neumann. This gives us dates for certain works of our Fritz and is an indicator when they started to work with each other.

item.title: Fritz Neumann-Hegenberg
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Even if Fritz Neumann-Hegenberg could be ruled out as “our” Fritz Neumann from the outset. There is further evidence to support this.

Already on 31 August 2021, three years ago, a work by Fritz Neumann-Hegenberg appeared on the TV programme “Bares für Rahres” . Following the programme, a newspaper article about the consequences was also published (behind a paywall).

His works are also represented in various online collections

  • In the MoMA Collection of German Expressionism
  • In the Museum of Cultural History in Görlitz

item.title: Fritz Neumann as a member of the Reichskunstkammer
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Since both the address book entries and some of Fritz Neumann’s works (such as this from August 1935 or this from between 1934 and 1951) date from the time of the ‘3rd Reich’, it is relatively likely that he was a member of the Reichskunstkammer . Membership was compulsory at the time…

And indeed, in the Landesarchiv Berlin (state archive Berlin), which administers the files of the “Reichskammer der bildenden Künste”, Landesleitung Berlin, there is a personal file on Fritz Neumann, born on 18 June 1905, under the archive signature A Rep. 243-04 No. 6261 !

item.title: Fritz Neumann (1928–2014) is not Ric!
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Fritz Neumann (1928–2014) is not Ric!

During my vacation I did some research on one of the last posts : I’ve contacted the Freudeskreis Kunst Oldenburg . They forwarded my questions to Andreas Neumann, the son of Fritz Neumann (1928–2014).

He send me the following reply:

Unfortunately, my father - Fritz Neumann - is not identical with the painter ‘Ric’. The handwriting and painting style do not match, and the Berlin address does not fit either. We lived in Ohlenstedt at the time and then moved to Oldenburg.
Andreas Neumann

Original in German:

Mein Vater - Fritz Neumann - ist leider nicht identisch mit dem Maler “Ric”. Schrift und Malstil stimmen nicht überein, und auch die angeführte Berliner Adresse paßt nicht. Wir haben zu der Zeit in Ohlenstedt gewohnt und sind dann nach Oldenburg gezogen.
Andreas Neumann

item.title: What are those prints worth?
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Due to popular demand (this question is responsible for 90% of inquiries), I’ll try to answer the question:

What are prints of Ric worth?

This question is hard to answer accuratetly. Since these prints aren’t numbered, it is not immediately obvious that they are actually not that rare. At least not in the north of Germany.

Based on my own experience:

  • A typical price on a flea market is between 10€ and 25€
  • In a junk or thrift shop you can get those for 20€ to 40€

Keep in mind that these prices apply on framed sheets, so a unframed sheet is worth from 10€ to 30€

item.title: Kunstverlag J.C. Blumenberg
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
The “Kunstverlag (fine art publisher) J.C. Blumenberg” was the publishing house for prints by Ric and Fritz Neumann. There are two embossing marks known.

From what we currently know, it’s almost certain, that the first one is the older one. Two main arguments are in favour of this:

  • There are far more print showing the second mark.
  • From the history of the publisher it is know to have changed location several times, especially after the second world war. Initially located in Lübeck, Germany. The logo / stamp mark around that time certainly showed a famous landmark from this city .

During the course of the search for Ric these marks were the first hint on the connection between Ric and Fritz Neumann. Since one of these also show the Holsten Gate in Lübeck, a connection towards Lübeck was suspected.

item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
The Fritz Neumann trace was originally discovered by Simon : Fritz Neumann used the same paper stamp mark (posts which feature some detail photographs of the stamp mark are tagged ).

It’s not clear yet, what this mark means. It could be added by the paper manufacturer (not very likely since in some cases it looks like it has been applied after the printing process), the printer or maybe it’s a sign of the printing studio.

item.title: A clue from the old blog
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Merry Christmas everyone!

Finally it’s the time in year to eat cookies and do some personal research. I found the following comment on the original blog by Simon .

I have over 30 different lithographs of the unknown artist RIC. Likewise I have in my collection 15 lithographs, which are signed with Fritz Neumann. The lithographs of both artists not only have the same embossing stamp “JCB” but show too clear similarities in motifs (boats, birds, lanes) as well as in brushstrokes. The only artist I know who also uses the stamp “JCB” is Han van Meegeren. In addition, I recognize in his lithograph “deer with fawn” left in the background a boat, as we know it in the style of Fritz Neumann and RIC. For several years I have been searching unsuccessfully for the artist RIC. On the back of some frames I recognized 8 stickers of art houses. I contacted each of them. Nobody can remember the artist RIC. My collection consists of more than 1000 works. None of these lithographs of other artits shows an embossing stamp “JCB”. Therefore the way to identify RIC leads over the embossing stamp of the printer. Does anyone know the embossing stamp and/or the printer? This would be very helpful in identifying the artist RIC. All information is highly appreciated.
Unknown Source

The link to the Blogger.com profile page might work if you have a Blogger.com account

item.title: Privacy policy
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Privacy policy

Hosting

The hoster collects the following data transmitted by your browser in log files:

  • IP address
  • The address of the previously visited website (Referer [sic!] request header)
  • Date and time of the enquiry
  • Time zone difference to Greenwich Mean Time
  • Content of the request
  • HTTP status code
  • Amount of data transferred
  • Website from which the request originates
  • Information about the browser and operating system

This is necessary to display the website and to ensure stability and security. This corresponds to a legitimate interest within the meaning of Art. 6 para. 1 sentence 1 lit. f GDPR .
